fieldNotes.location: Roster geocode (31.5795,-90.0394, address 1715 Highway 84 E) sat on Highway 84 in open forest ~5.6 km SSE of the actual mill - a city-level geocode error. Mill core relocated via CLUI/Global Energy Monitor coordinates and satellite to ~31.6282,-90.0815, on Na Sandifer Hwy (Old Highway 84) along the Pearl River, ~1 mile east of Monticello, Lawrence County MS.
fieldNotes.facility: Georgia-Pacific Monticello Mill - an integrated kraft pulp and linerboard (containerboard) mill. In 2024 it became one of few North American facilities to produce over 1 million tons of product. Subject of a $91M upgrade announced 2023 (Infor Phase 2 per dossier). Large campus: paper machine buildings, woodyard with two radial log/chip storage piles, wastewater treatment clarifiers and ponds, finished-goods shipping warehouse, rail yard, support structures.
fieldNotes.truckGate: TRUE - controlled mill entrance. The single mill access road branches NE off Na Sandifer Hwy (~31.6213,-90.0805) and runs ~400 m into the property; Street View (2024-03) shows signage, a posted entrance and an industrial checkpoint approach. A controlled, gated/scaled entrance is universal for an integrated paper mill receiving log/chip vans; gate structures sit at the property line beyond Street View coverage.
fieldNotes.guardShack: TRUE (medium confidence) - a small structure is visible at the entrance/scale area near 31.6236,-90.0838; consistent with a guard/scale house. Not pinpointed at high resolution - flagged.
fieldNotes.preGateStaging: Long access road and wide gravel aprons outside the gate; satellite shows trailers/trucks queued bumper-to-bumper along the entrance road - ample pre-gate waiting room.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large paved/gravel yard areas inside the gate before the docks and woodyard scales.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: The gate-to-dock approach is a long internal road (hundreds of meters) that easily holds a queue of 3+ trucks; a substantial truck queue was visible in imagery.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Very wide gravel entrance aprons and unused paved/graded width near the gate provide physical room for a bypass/express lane.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Receiving (woodyard log/chip vans, chemical and rail receiving) is physically separate from finished linerboard shipping at the warehouse dock bank on the NW side - distinct clusters.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Finished-goods shipping warehouse on the NW side shows a dock face with banks of doors and trailers backed in; counted band 10-25, medium confidence (roof shadow obscures exact count).
fieldNotes.dropArea: Extensive trailer drop yards: rows of dozens of parked trailers in the warehouse drop yard and additional trailers staged along the entrance road - well over 50 trailers visible, band 50+.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus: pulp/paper machine core, woodyard with two radial chip/log piles, wastewater treatment plant (clarifiers + multiple ponds), shipping warehouse, rail yard, plus numerous support buildings - 20+ distinct structures.
fieldNotes.railServed: TRUE - multiple rail spurs run directly into the property, serving the warehouse and woodyard; covered rail loading sheds and rail cars visible.
fieldNotes.scale: TRUE (medium confidence) - truck scales for chip/log van weigh-in are operationally required at an integrated paper mill of this scale; a scale-house-sized structure sits in the truck path near the entrance. Not resolved precisely - flagged.
fieldNotes.multiStep: Possible second checkpoint (gate then woodyard scale) but not clearly confirmed in imagery - left false, flagged.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Monticello is a small Mississippi town; the mill sits on the edge of town surrounded by forest and the Pearl River. Rural.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~320 acres for the full fenced industrial property including warehouse, mill core, woodyard and treatment ponds; honest estimate from the perimeter box.

citations.claim: GP Monticello linerboard mill surpassed 1M tons/yr; $91M upgrade underway

verification.rationale: GP-owned, record production, 2025 GP confirmation; named Cedar Springs volume recipient.
